Problems Identified
P1
Urban Heat Island Effect
Critical Thermal
Evidence from Analysis
Peak surface temperature 47°C recorded over Galle Road pavement (Landsat 8 thermal band)
UTCI mean of 39°C — classified as Very Strong Heat Stress zone during midday
62% of the study area classified as high heat stress zone
OSR critically low at 0.05 in commercial core — near-zero permeable ground surface
FSI peaks of 2.1 along Galle Road block coastal sea breeze penetration
Linked Analyses
🌡 UTCI Map 🗺 Heat Map 📐 FSI Analysis 📊 OSR Grid 💨 Wind Simulation
Planning Recommendations
01
Green corridor along Galle Road — mandate street tree planting every 8m, continuous canopy to reduce surface temp by est. 4–6°C
02
Cool roof incentive programme — retrofit high-albedo roofing on commercial buildings with FSI > 1.8
03
Permeable paving requirement — all new developments in high-GSI zones must dedicate ≥30% permeable surface
Severity
Critical
Urgency
Immediate
Scale
Area-wide
P2
Severe Junction Traffic Congestion
Critical Mobility
Evidence from Analysis
Highest betweenness centrality at 5000m radius along Galle Road — regional through-traffic dominates local streets
Closeness at 500m shows the junction as the most accessible local node — but pedestrian access is blocked by vehicle lanes
No grade-separated pedestrian crossings at the main junction intersection
Conflict between rail-level crossing, bus stops, and private vehicles at a single chokepoint
Linked Analyses
📍 Betweenness 5000m 📍 Closeness 500m 🗺 Land Use Map
Planning Recommendations
01
Junction redesign — introduce dedicated pedestrian phase and bus priority lane at the Galle Road / Station Road intersection
02
Through-traffic diversion — create alternative parallel route to offload regional traffic from Galle Road within the study area
Severity
Critical
Urgency
Immediate
Scale
Junction
P3
Critically Fragmented Open Space
Critical Liveability
Evidence from Analysis
OSR in commercial core as low as 0.05 — one of the lowest recorded in Sri Lankan urban contexts
Only 13.3 ha of public space across the entire 538 ha study area (2.5%)
Existing open space clusters only at the south-eastern wetland edge — inaccessible from the main junction
GSI of 0.72 in the core means buildings cover 72% of the ground plane
Linked Analyses
📐 OSR Grid 📐 GSI Map 🗺 Land Use Map 📊 UMI Index
Planning Recommendations
01
Mandatory OSR standard — require minimum OSR of 0.25 for all new commercial developments > 500m²
02
Pocket parks network — convert underutilised parcels and setbacks into a connected green network linking station to seafront
Severity
Critical
Urgency
Short-term
Scale
Area-wide
P4
Uneven Urban Maturation Pressure
Critical Urban Form
Evidence from Analysis
UMI of 0.78 in commercial core vs 0.41 in residential edge — a steep transition gradient
High FSI (2.1) and GSI (0.72) in the core vs low OSR (0.05) indicates over-development without amenity
Residential edges undergoing rapid infill without infrastructure upgrade — mismatch with UMI gradient
Sri Saranankara GN: density 17,019 persons/km² — highest in study area with minimal public space
Linked Analyses
📊 UMI Map 📐 FSI Analysis 👥 Population Density
Planning Recommendations
01
Graduated density zoning — introduce transition zones with stepped FSI limits between core and edge to manage maturation gradient
02
Infrastructure-first infill policy — require infrastructure capacity assessment before approving residential densification in edge GN divisions
Severity
Critical
Urgency
Short-term
Scale
Area-wide
P5
Poor Pedestrian Connectivity
Moderate Mobility
Evidence from Analysis
High 500m closeness centrality shows strong walkable potential — but discontinuous footpaths prevent realisation
Street-level wind simulation shows heat stress worsens at ground level where pedestrian activity is highest
Jayathilaka GN (density 10,970/km²) has lowest closeness — residents must route through congested junction
Linked Analyses
📍 Closeness 500m 💨 Wind Simulation 👥 Population Map
Planning Recommendations
01
Shaded pedestrian network — design shaded walkways connecting station to Galle Road with canopy coverage ≥70%
02
Block-level connectivity audit — identify and open pedestrian shortcuts through blocks to reduce walking distances
Severity
Moderate
Urgency
Short-term
Scale
Junction
P6
Inadequate Sanitation in Dense GN Zones
Moderate Infrastructure
Evidence from Analysis
Galwala GN: 9 households with no toilet facilities — highest in study area at density 12,278/km²
Jayathilaka GN: 54 households using kerosene — infrastructure gap in otherwise electrified area
Shared toilet usage concentrated in Nedimala (65 hh) and Vilawala (64 hh) — high-density zones
Linked Analyses
👥 Census Data 👥 Population Density
Planning Recommendations
01
Targeted sanitation upgrade — prioritise Galwala and Jayathilaka GNs for subsidised toilet and utility connections
02
Community facility mapping — identify locations for shared sanitation blocks in high-density low-income clusters
Severity
Moderate
Urgency
Short-term
Scale
GN-level
Key Potentials & Opportunities
K1
Strong Walkable Local Accessibility
High Value Mobility
Evidence
500m closeness centrality ranks Dehiwala Junction as the highest accessibility node in the study area
Dense mixed-use base within walkable radius means most daily needs can theoretically be met on foot
High Shannon Entropy near the station shows existing variety of land uses supporting active frontages
How to Leverage
→
Reclaim pavement from parked vehicles and widen footpaths along the top 3 closeness streets to create a walkable commercial spine
→
Market Dehiwala as a 15-minute neighbourhood — low car-dependency model within existing urban structure
K2
Transit-Ready Mixed Land Use Base
High Value Land Use
Evidence
Shannon Entropy Index of 0.72 near the station — among the highest in the study area, indicating genuine land use diversity
12 distinct land use categories present within a 500m radius of Dehiwala station
Commercial, residential, institutional and cultural uses all within walkable distance of the rail stop
How to Leverage
→
Develop a Transit-Oriented Development (TOD) masterplan centred on Dehiwala station — protect land use mix while enabling vertical densification
→
Designate a 400m TOD zone with mixed-use zoning overlays protecting ground-floor retail and active uses
K3
Regional Connectivity Asset
Strategic Connectivity
Evidence
5000m betweenness centrality identifies Dehiwala as a key node on the Colombo–South Coast corridor
Rail connection provides direct access to Colombo Fort, Mount Lavinia and Kalutara
2000m betweenness shows secondary connections to Nugegoda and Kohuwala commercial nodes
How to Leverage
→
Position Dehiwala as a sub-regional service centre — attract higher-order commercial, health and education facilities enabled by regional accessibility
→
Coordinate with Western Province transport planning to designate Dehiwala as a bus-rail interchange node
K4
Under-Utilised Rail Catchment for TOD
Strategic Transit
Evidence
Dehiwala station is on the mainline Colombo–Galle railway — high-frequency service, central location
Current station forecourt is dominated by informal parking — not utilised as a transit-oriented public space
800m walking catchment covers majority of the study area — effectively the entire population is within rail access
How to Leverage
→
Station forecourt redesign — convert informal parking to an active public plaza with shade, seating and last-mile connectivity (cycling, tuk-tuks)
→
Enable mixed-use intensification within 400m of station entrance — residential above ground-floor commercial to increase ridership and housing supply
K5
Southeastern Wetland as Cooling Anchor
Environmental Green Infra
Evidence
OSR of 0.65 in the southeastern wetland zone — the only major open permeable surface in the study area
Surface temperatures in coastal/wetland zone approx 32°C vs 47°C at Galle Road — 15°C differential
Sea breeze corridor from the southwest identified in wind simulation — wetland acts as cooling relay point
How to Leverage
→
Protect and extend wetland edge — designate buffer zone with no-build setback and native planting to enhance evapotranspiration and air cooling
→
Design a green breeze corridor connecting wetland to the station via a tree-lined public path — channelling cool air into the urban core
